blocks.text: Living in Chilliwack River Valley

parts.t: The Chilliwack River Valley is the area the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) describes as Electoral Area E, in the North Cascade mountains. BC Parks places Chilliwack Lake Park 64 km southeast of Chilliwack. The valley is not inside the City. The FVRD says Area E had 1,568 people in the 2021 Census and covers 652 square kilometres.

The FVRD’s slope study covers the slopes on both sides of the Chilliwack River valley, from Baker Trails in the east to the Slesse Park landslide in the west, plus the Ranger Run area and the Post Creek subdivision. It names Baker Trails, Bell Acres, Slesse Park and Post Creek as communities in the valley.
No official document gives street-by-street boundaries, and Chilliwack Lake Road is the road that runs up the valley. See all

parts.t: Chilliwack is in School District 33 (SD33). SD33’s Long Range Facilities Plan says its elementary schools are kindergarten to grade 5, its middle schools grades 6 to 8 and its secondary schools grades 9 to 12.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Chilliwack River Valley

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H is FVRD Bylaw No. 1115, 2011. The FVRD’s housing report says it was adopted in 2011 for the former Electoral Area E and amended in 2019 to recognize the split of that area into Area E and Area H.

The FVRD says an Official Community Plan amendment for Electoral Areas E and H was adopted in January 2021, at the same time as the Popkum-Bridal Falls plan. It put in place the findings of two reports in the Chilliwack River Valley about the Erosion Setback Line in the Wilson Road to Baker Trails area and the Slesse Park area.

Slope: the FVRD’s Chilliwack River Valley Slope Stability Risk Assessment, with BGC Engineering, is funded by the Province’s Ministry of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness. It looks at landslides, debris flows, rotational slumps, rockfall and rockslides on both sides of the valley, and focuses on these geohazards rather than flooding or wildfires.

The FVRD’s project page, last updated December 6, 2025, says a survey received 108 responses and a community workshop in the valley was planned for the winter. No separate project notice is listed in the current online directory.
Dikes and water: the FVRD lists Dyke Operations and Maintenance, Storm Drainage, Transit and Water among Electoral Area E’s local services.

Flood: Chilliwack River Provincial Park has floodplain characteristics, per BC Parks. Published municipal records do not list property-level floodplain mapping for the valley, so check the address with the FVRD.
ALR: Published municipal records do not list an area-wide ALR figure for the valley. ALR status is parcel-specific, so check the exact parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission map.

Transit: BC Transit’s Transit Future Action Plan lists nine routes in the Chilliwack Conventional Transit system and describes it as service within the City of Chilliwack. Published municipal records list no fixed-route bus into the valley.

The Chilliwack River Valley is outside the City of Chilliwack, so City zoning does not apply. The FVRD sets zoning for Electoral Area E. Send me the address and I’ll point you to the right FVRD rules.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Chilliwack River Valley

parts.t: Confirm the local government and rules.
The valley is in FVRD Electoral Area E, so ask the FVRD, not the City, about zoning and building.
Check the slope and the erosion setback.
Ask the FVRD whether the parcel is near the river, the Erosion Setback Line areas or a mapped slope hazard before you plan any building.
Ask about water and septic.
Confirm how the property is served and what the septic system looks like before you count on a suite or an addition.
Plan your drive.
There is no fixed-route bus into the valley, so think about winter driving and the distance to schools and shops.
Confirm the school catchment.
There is no school in the valley, so use the SD33 School Locator for the exact address.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, plumbing, wiring and any septic system.

blocks.text: Chilliwack River Valley questions

parts.t: Where is the Chilliwack River Valley?
The FVRD describes Electoral Area E, in the North Cascade mountains, as the area known as the Chilliwack River Valley, with 1,568 people in the 2021 Census across 652 square kilometres.

The FVRD’s slope study covers both sides of the valley from Baker Trails in the east to the Slesse Park landslide in the west, plus the Ranger Run area and the Post Creek subdivision, and names Baker Trails, Bell Acres, Slesse Park and Post Creek as communities.
Ask me if a specific address is in it.
How do I get around from the Chilliwack River Valley?

Published municipal records list no fixed-route BC Transit bus into the valley. BC Transit’s Transit Future Action Plan lists nine routes in the Chilliwack system and describes it as service within the City of Chilliwack.
BC Transit’s Rider’s Guide says residents of the Chilliwack River Valley and Cultus Lake North may be eligible for handyDART, its door-to-door service for people who can’t use fixed-route buses.
Which school is in the Chilliwack River Valley?
No SD33 school is in the valley. The Province’s list of School District 33 schools shows no school with a Chilliwack Lake Road or valley address.
Use the official directory or SD33 School Locator to confirm which schools valley addresses are assigned to. Check an exact address with the
SD33 School Locator
What parks and library are in the valley?
Thompson Regional Park (48600 Chilliwack Lake Road) is a 3-hectare FVRD park with a picnic shelter, playground and 1 km loop trail.
Sx̱ótsaqel / Chilliwack Lake Provincial Park has 182 frontcountry campsites, 64 km southeast of Chilliwack.
The nearest library is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road. Published municipal records list no library branch in the valley.
What plan covers the valley?

The Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H is FVRD Bylaw No. 1115, 2011. The FVRD’s housing report says it was adopted in 2011 for the former Electoral Area E and amended in 2019 to recognize the split of that area into Area E and Area H.
A 2021 amendment put in place two reports’ findings on the Erosion Setback Line in the Wilson Road to Baker Trails area and the Slesse Park area.
Is the valley a flood or landslide area?
The FVRD is running a slope stability risk assessment for the valley with BGC Engineering, covering landslides, debris flows, rotational slumps, rockfall and rockslides.
BC Parks says Chilliwack River Provincial Park has floodplain characteristics.
Published municipal records do not list property-level floodplain mapping. Ask me or the FVRD about a specific lot.
What are the homes and lots like?
Most housing units in Electoral Areas E and H combined are single detached (78%), and movable dwellings make up 21%. These figures are not for the valley alone.
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
Agricultural Land Commission map
. Lot size (FVREB MLS® recorded sales data): the median lot size of detached houses sold in recent 2026 MLS® activity was 20,691 sq ft (about 0.5 acre), based on 4 sales with a recorded lot size.
That is only 4 sales. In my size bands, acreage is 1 to 10 acres. About 0.5 acre is below the acreage band, so treat this as a regular large lot, not an acreage.
